name: Leonardo da Vinci
hook: The Renaissance man Jeopardy asks about most: two paintings, one drawing, and a very famous smile.

facts.label: the Mona Lisa
facts.statement: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre; Leonardo never delivered it to the sitter, and it was sold to the king of France around 1520.

facts.label: The Last Supper
facts.statement: The Last Supper is a mural in the refectory of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, commissioned by Ludovico Sforza; Judas is the apostle who spills the salt.

facts.label: Vitruvian Man
facts.statement: The Vitruvian Man, drawn around 1490, applies proportions set down by the Roman architect Vitruvius; Italy put the drawing on its euro coins.

facts.label: Milan and Ludovico Sforza
facts.statement: Leonardo left Florence around 1482 to serve Ludovico Sforza, duke of Milan, pitching himself as a maker of armored wagons and sculpture.

facts.label: Vinci, Tuscany
facts.statement: Leonardo was born in 1452 near Vinci, a small Tuscan hill town, and trained as an artist in Florence.

facts.label: Salvator Mundi
facts.statement: Salvator Mundi sold for 45 pounds in 1958 and $450 million in 2017, after it was attributed to Leonardo.

facts.label: the Louvre holdings
facts.statement: The Louvre owns several Leonardos beyond the Mona Lisa, including the Virgin of the Rocks and St. John the Baptist.
